subject.title: fix(agents): terminate mixed tool-call batches on critical loop veto

question: Should a critical tool-loop veto end the run before accepted steering and follow-up input is drained, and should this PR be selected as the canonical implementation over https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106297?
rationale: Both candidate PRs use the same broad termination shape, but the queue lifecycle is an intentional session and message-delivery contract that source inspection cannot safely choose for maintainers.

options.title: Preserve and resume queued input
options.body: Select one canonical PR only after it ensures accepted queued input is automatically processed by a safe subsequent run or explicitly re-enqueued at the owning session boundary.

options.title: Accept deferred delivery
options.body: Select one canonical PR and explicitly approve that queued input remains pending until another prompt is started on the same Agent instance, with production proof of that lifecycle.

options.title: Pause both candidates
options.body: Keep both PRs unselected until a narrower termination design avoids changing accepted-input handling or stronger runtime evidence establishes the intended contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve and resume queued input
recommendation.body: Select one canonical PR only after it ensures accepted queued input is automatically processed by a safe subsequent run or explicitly re-enqueued at the owning session boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history on the Agent wrapper and loop lifecycle makes them the strongest available owner for choosing the terminal and queued-input semantics.
